key_claims: Older adults who followed the Mediterranean diet more closely had higher blood concentrations of the mitochondrial microproteins humanin and SHMOOSE.
Higher humanin levels were linked to eating more olive oil, fish, and legumes, while higher SHMOOSE levels were associated with consuming olive oil and fewer refined carbohydrates.
Participants with higher adherence to the Mediterranean diet exhibited lower markers of oxidative stress.
Higher humanin levels were associated with lower activity of the Nox2 enzyme, which is involved in generating reactive oxygen species.
limitations: The study was relatively small and observational, so it cannot prove that the Mediterranean diet directly causes an increase in humanin or SHMOOSE levels.
The observed associations do not confirm that these microproteins directly prevent cardiovascular disease or cognitive decline.
Unmeasured factors such as overall health status and other lifestyle habits could have influenced the biological measurements.
what_not_to_say: Do not state that eating a Mediterranean diet is proven to increase humanin or SHMOOSE levels.
Do not claim that humanin or SHMOOSE directly prevent Alzheimer's disease or heart attacks.
Do not present the findings as a clinical trial or definitive proof of causal biological mechanisms.
